newsitem.title: UK: IRA guerrillas abandon mine in Northern Ireland.
newsitem.headline: IRA guerrillas abandon mine in Northern Ireland.

text.p: Outlawed IRA guerrillas said on Saturday they had abandoned a landmine in a Catholic area of west Belfast after first defusing it.

A telephone caller using an Irish Republican Army identity codeword told Downtown radio station that their fighters had dumped the device "because of civilian activity in the area." The operation was the first by the IRA in Northern Ireland since Labour's landslide election win on May 1.

The telephone caller did not specify the target. The IRA has frequently placed landmines in nationalist Catholic areas aimed at passing British security force patrols in the predominantly Protestant province.
The caller said the IRA's "engineers" had made the bomb safe before abandoning it. Police said that they were aware of the phone call but gave no further details.

Shortly after winning power new Prime Minister Tony Blair allowed the resumption of talks between government officials and the IRA's Sinn Fein political wing in a bid to end the province's long running guerrilla war stalemate.
But Blair made clear the talks could only take place if the IRA refrained from using violence. Two rounds of talks have been held in the past ten days and another is due soon.
